title: Duration between rewards controls the rate of behavioral and dopaminergic learning
goal: Reproduce the original reward-spacing effects on behavioral learning trajectories and dopamine responses, and the elapsed-time-versus-trial-count comparisons, using the source-defined animal cohorts, schedules, onset definitions and indispensable controls for the named result. Preserve the source's limits on proportional scaling and distinguish behavior-only from photometry support. Report Figure 5's five-ITI model-fit comparison as a separately named empirical modeling component; a better fit alone does not reproduce or improve the biological family. Assess improvement of the same primary finding only under an independently justified criterion.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Named central reward-spacing effects on behavioral learning and dopamine, with elapsed-time-versus-trial-count comparisons and source-specific controls. The retained next action names one matched contrast whose exact panel remains unbound; no automatic all-18-figure or whole-paper requirement.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained source work: empirical_modeling_component: Figure 5's five-ITI trials-to-learn comparison is genuine modeling of real behavioral observations using TDRL, SOP and ANCCR simulations. Retain complete selected source conditions, log-RSS selection and separately reported AIC variants; fit quality cannot substitute for biological or dopamine reproduction.
interpretive_model_control: Original model comparisons remain companion evidence when the named mechanistic interpretation requires them; they are not universally compulsory for every narrower empirical result.
prospective_extension: New animal-held-out splits, rewritten penalties, new learning metrics or newly selected candidate-model evaluation policies remain extensions and require separate scientific justification.
